transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've been getting out of breath climbing the stairs. It's been getting worse over about three months now, and it's worrying me.
Do you have any allergies, or have you ever had a bad reaction to a medicine?
No, I've never had any allergies to medicines that I know of.
How much does getting out of breath when you climb the stairs affect your day-to-day life?
Well, I have to stop halfway up the stairs now to catch my breath — there are 14 of them — and I used to manage without stopping. It worries me, especially since our bedroom is upstairs.
What medicines are you taking at the moment, and have any been started or changed recently?
I take rivaroxaban 15 mg once a day with my evening meal, bisoprolol 5 mg once a day, atorvastatin 40 mg at night, and ramipril 2.5 mg once a day. As far as I know, nothing's been changed recently.
Do you have any health conditions that you've had for a long time?
I've had atrial fibrillation for about 5 years now, and I had a heart attack 12 years ago.
How bad is the breathlessness when you climb the stairs — is it mild, moderate, or severe, or are you not sure?
I'd say it's moderate — I have to stop halfway up the 14 stairs to get my breath back, and I never used to need to do that.
When you get out of breath on the stairs, do you notice anything else happening at the same time?
My ankles get a bit puffy in the evening, and I've started using two pillows instead of one at night. I don't get any chest pain, and I haven't been coughing up blood or had a fever.
Where in your body do you feel that breathlessness most when you're climbing the stairs?
I can't say I've noticed it in any particular spot — it's just a general feeling of not being able to get enough air when I'm climbing.
Over the last few weeks, has this breathlessness been with you all the time, or does it come and go?
It comes and goes — it only happens when I'm on the stairs or walking uphill, and it settles after I rest for two or three minutes. I'm not breathless when I'm sitting still.
When that feeling of not being able to get enough air comes on, how would you describe it to me in your own words?
It's like I've run out of puff and can't get my breath back quickly — I just have to stop and let it settle. It's not painful, just a real struggle to breathe until I rest.
Besides the two past health issues you mentioned, is there anything else — other long-term conditions, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays — that you’d like to add?
I had a heart scan — an echocardiogram — at the hospital last year, but I'm afraid I can't remember what the result was. Otherwise, nothing else I can think of.
Is there anything else you’d like to add about your medicines?
No, I don't think so — that's all the medicines I take.
Is there anything else you've noticed when you get out of breath on the stairs?
No, I don't think there's anything else I've noticed.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
